In [[representation theory]], a '''Jantzen filtration''' is a [[Filtration_(mathematics)|filtration]] of a [[Verma module]] of a [[semisimple Lie algebra]], or a [[Weyl module]] of a [[reductive algebraic group]] of positive characteristic. Jantzen filtrations were introduced by {{harvs|txt|author-link=Jens Carsten Jantzen|last=Jantzen|year=1979}}.

==Jantzen filtration for Verma modules==

If ''M''(λ) is a Verma module of a semisimple Lie algebra with highest weight λ, then the Janzen filtration is a decreasing filtration
:<math>M(\lambda)=M(\lambda)^0\supseteq M(\lambda)^1\supseteq M(\lambda)^2\supseteq\cdots.</math>
It has the following properties:
*''M''(λ)<sup>1</sup>=''N''(λ), the unique maximal proper submodule of ''M''(λ)
*The quotients ''M''(λ)<sup>''i''</sup>/''M''(λ)<sup>''i''+1</sup> have non-degenerate [[contravariant form|contravariant bilinear forms]].
* The '''Jantzen sum formula''' holds: 
:<math>\sum_{i>0}\text{Ch}(M(\lambda)^i) = \sum_{\alpha>0, s_\alpha(\lambda)<\lambda}\text{Ch}(M(s_\alpha \cdot \lambda))</math>
: where <math>\text{Ch}(\cdot)</math> denotes the [[Algebraic character|formal character]].
